brief: Goldman added a 25bp hike at this week's September FOMC to its forecast on Friday after the August CPI report. The report changed little in its inflation view, but it pushed market pricing of a hike to nearly 90 percent, high enough that the FOMC will likely deliver rather than absorb the reaction to holding. Goldman sees no strong economic case. All of the overshoot of the 2 percent target is attributed to fading one-time factors, core PCE ran near a 2.5 percent annualized pace from June through August, breadth looks normal once tariff effects are netted out, expectations are not near unanchoring, and its bottlenecks tracker shows no overheating. It therefore expects the FOMC to signal nothing further, making only the minimum statement change, with Waller dissenting and Warsh using press conference language such as carefully assess to cool October pricing already near 50 percent. The dots are expected to show a 10-8 majority for one 2026 hike, with a risk of two. Goldman keeps two 2027 cuts, moved to September and December, raises the terminal rate to 3.25-3.5 percent, and holds a probability-weighted path considerably less hawkish than market pricing.
